items.stem: Explain the common defects of eye, their causes and methods of correction.
items.answer:
The four most common types of defects of vision are :
(a) Myopia or near-sightedness. Causes of myopia : this defect arises due to either of the following two reasons — (i) the distance of the retina from the eye lens increases, (ii) the focal length of the eye lens becomes small. Correction of myopia : this defect can be corrected by using a concave lens of appropriate focal length.
(b) Hypermetropia or far-sightedness. Causes of hypermetropia : this defect arises due to either of the following two reasons — (i) the distance of the retina from the eye lens decreases, (ii) the focal length of the eye lens becomes large. Correction of hypermetropia : this defect can be corrected by a convex lens of appropriate power (or focal length).
(c) Presbyopia. Causes of presbyopia : this defect arises because the power of accommodation of the eye decreases due to the gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing of flexibility of the eye lens. Correction of presbyopia : this defect can be corrected by using bi-focal lenses. Its lower part consists of a convex lens which is used for reading purposes, whereas the upper part consists of a concave lens which is used for distant vision.
(d) Astigmatism. Causes of astigmatism : this defect is usually due to the cornea, which is not perfectly spherical and has different curvatures for horizontally and vertically lying objects. Correction of astigmatism : it can be corrected by using cylindrical lenses.

items.stem: With the help of ciliary muscles the human eye can change its curvature and thus alter the focal length of its lens. State the changes that occur in the curvature and focal length of the eye lens while viewing (i) a distant object, (ii) a nearby object. Explain, why a normal eye is not able to see distinctly the objects placed closer than 25 cm, without putting any strain on the eye.
items.answer:
(i) When we see distant objects, the ciliary muscles relax to decrease the curvature and thereby increase the focal length of the lens. Hence, the lens becomes thin. This enables us to see the distant object clearly. Thus, the focal length of the eye lens increases while seeing distant objects.
(ii) To see nearby objects clearly, the focal length of the lens should be shorter. For this, the ciliary muscles contract to increase the curvature and thereby decrease the focal length of the lens. Hence, the lens becomes thick. This enables us to see nearby objects clearly.
A normal eye is not able to see distinctly the objects placed closer than 25 cm without putting any strain on the eye. This is because the ciliary muscles of the eye are unable to contract beyond a certain limit; if the object is placed at a distance less than 25 cm from the eye, then the object appears blurred because the light rays coming from the object meet beyond the retina.

items.stem: The apparent altitude of stars appears to be generally more than their true altitudes. Explain, how.
items.answer: As we go up and up in the earth's atmosphere, it goes on becoming rarer and rarer. As a result, the atmospheric layer near the earth's surface has the maximum refractive index and the refractive index gradually decreases with increase in height. When a light ray from a star enters the earth's atmosphere, it travels from a rarer to a denser medium and hence continues to bend towards the normal. As a result, an observer on the earth considers the apparent position of the star to be at a higher altitude than its true position.

items.stem: Write about power of accommodation of human eye. Explain why the image distance in the eye does not change when we change the distance of an object from the eye ?
items.answer: The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called power of accommodation. The focal length of the eye lens is adjusted so that the image distance does not change. Thus, the image distance is always equal to the distance from the centre of the eye lens to the retina.

items.stem: A student finds the writing on the blackboard as blurred and unclear when sitting on the last desk of the classroom. He however sees clearly when sitting on the front desk at an approximate distance 2 m from the blackboard. (a) Draw the ray diagram to illustrate the formation of image of the blackboard writing by his eye lens when he sits at the : (i) last desk (ii) front desk. (b) Name the defect of vision the student is suffering from. Also list two causes of this defect. (c) Name the kind of lens that would enable him to see clearly when he is seated at the last desk. Draw the ray diagram to illustrate how this lens helps him to see clearly.
items.answer:
(a) (i) When the student sits at the last desk, the image of the blackboard writing is formed in front of (before) the retina by his eye lens, so the writing appears blurred. (ii) When he sits at the front desk, 2 m away, the image is formed exactly on the retina and the writing is seen clearly. (Ray diagrams as shown.)
(b) The student is suffering from myopia. Causes : (i) elongation of the eye ball, (ii) excessive curvature of the cornea.
(c) A concave lens of suitable focal length can be used for correction. The concave lens diverges the rays from the distant blackboard before they enter the eye, so the eye lens now forms the image on the retina.
items.ocr: Both figures printed with this item are solution ray diagrams, so none is attached to the question.

items.stem: A person cannot see the objects distinctly, when placed beyond 2 m. (a) Identify the eye defect. (b) Give two reasons for this defect. (c) Calculate the power and nature of the lens he should be using to see the distant objects clearly. (d) Draw the ray diagrams for the defective and the corrected eyes.
items.answer:
(a) Myopia (near-sightedness).
(b) Reasons for this defect : (i) either the power of the eye lens has become more than its normal value due to excessive curvature of the cornea, or (ii) elongation of the eye ball due to some genetic defect.
(c) The far point is 2 m, so the corrective lens must bring an object at infinity to 2 m in front of the eye, i.e. f = −2 m.
P = 1/f = 1/(−2 m) = −0.5 D.
The power is −0.5 D and the lens is a concave (diverging) lens.
(d) Ray diagrams for the defective eye (image formed in front of the retina) and for the corrected eye (concave lens shifts the image onto the retina).

items.stem: A person wears spectacles of power −2.5 D. Name the defect of vision he is suffering from. Draw the ray diagram for (i) the defective eye, (ii) its correction after using a suitable lens.
items.answer: Since the power of the lens is negative, the lens used is a concave lens. Therefore the person is suffering from myopia or short-sightedness. Ray diagrams : (i) for the defective (myopic) eye the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina; (ii) after placing the concave lens of power −2.5 D before the eye, the rays are diverged so that the eye lens forms the image on the retina.

items.stem: A person can read the number plate of a distant bus clearly but he finds difficulty in reading a book. What type of defect of vision he is suffering from ? Name the type of lens he needs to correct this defect. Write the causes of this defect.
items.answer: He is suffering from hypermetropia (far-sightedness). A convex lens of suitable focal length is required to correct this defect. Causes of hypermetropia : (i) the focal length of the eye lens is too long, (ii) the eye ball has become too small.

items.stem: (a) State two main causes of developing farsightedness. (b) How can this defect of vision be corrected ?
items.answer:
(a) (i) The eye ball is too small. (ii) The focal length of the eye lens is too large.
(b) This eye defect is corrected by using a convex lens of suitable focal length, which converges the rays from a nearby object so that the image falls on the retina.

items.stem: What are the causes of the following defects of vision and how can they be corrected ? (a) Cataract (b) Presbyopia.
items.answer:
(a) Cataract : sometimes the crystalline lens becomes milky and cloudy in old age. This causes partial or complete loss of eyesight. Correction : through a cataract surgery.
(b) Presbyopia : the power of accommodation of the eye decreases with age, so the near point recedes away. It is due to the weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens. In this defect a person may suffer from both myopia and hypermetropia. Correction : by wearing spectacles having bifocal lenses.

items.stem: A child is able to read his book comfortably but is unable to read the matter written on the blackboard at certain distance. (a) Name the defect of vision he is suffering from. (b) With the help of labelled ray diagram show (i) the above mentioned defect of vision, (ii) correction of the above mentioned defect using a suitable lens.
items.answer:
(a) Myopia (short-sightedness).
(b) A concave lens of negative power is used for correction. (i) In the myopic eye the rays from the distant blackboard are brought to a focus in front of the retina, so the writing is blurred. (ii) With a concave lens of suitable focal length placed before the eye, the rays diverge before entering the eye and the eye lens now forms the image on the retina.

items.stem: What is atmospheric refraction ? Use this phenomenon to explain the following natural events : (a) Twinkling of stars, (b) Advanced sun-rise and delayed sun-set. Draw diagrams to illustrate your answers.
items.answer:
Atmospheric refraction : the refraction of light caused by the earth's atmosphere (having air layers of varying optical densities) is called atmospheric refraction.
(a) Twinkling of stars : atmospheric pressure (and hence density) keeps on decreasing considerably with altitude, so the upper layers of the atmosphere are optically rarer than the lower layers. The rays of light suffer refraction at each layer of the atmosphere and bend slightly. Thus, each ray of light from the star follows a curved path to reach the observer; a ray from a star at X appears to come from a star at X′, i.e. the star appears to be higher in the sky. Due to wind and convection currents, the density of the atmospheric layers keeps on changing, so the apparent position of the star keeps fluctuating about its mean position. This fluctuating image of the star makes it appear to twinkle to the observer.
(b) Advanced sunrise and delayed sunset : the sun is visible before the actual sunrise and after the actual sunset. Air near the earth is optically denser than that at higher altitudes. The sun's rays, while travelling to reach the surface of the earth, suffer refraction at each layer as they travel from a rarer to a denser medium. Due to these bent rays, the sun appears higher above the horizon than it actually is. Therefore the sun becomes visible about 2 minutes before its actual sunrise and remains visible for about 2 minutes after its actual sunset.

items.stem: (a) What is meant by dispersion of white light ? Describe the formation of rainbow in the sky with the help of a diagram. (b) What is hypermetropia ? Draw ray diagrams to show the image formation of an object by (i) Hypermetropic eye. (ii) Correction made with a suitable lens for hypermetropic eye.
items.answer:
(a) Dispersion : the process of splitting of white light into its seven constituent colours is called dispersion. The band of seven colours formed on a screen due to the dispersion of white light is called the spectrum of visible light (spectrum of white light).
Rainbow : the rainbow is the spectrum of sunlight in nature. When the atmosphere is heavily moisture laden (at the time of rain), spherical water droplets act as prisms and refract the sunlight to lead to the formation of a rainbow. Parallel beams of light coming from the sun get dispersed at the first surface of a water droplet, suffer total internal reflection at the second surface and are refracted again on emerging, producing a cone of rays at the observer's eye. The rainbow therefore appears as an arc of a circle for an observer on the earth.
(b) Hypermetropia (long-sightedness) is the defect of the human eye in which a person can see clearly objects at large distances, but cannot see nearby objects clearly. In such an eye the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina. Correction : it is corrected by using spectacles having a convex lens, which converges the rays and shifts the image from beyond the retina on to the retina. A person suffering from both myopia and hypermetropia has to wear spectacles having bifocal lenses — the upper half is a concave lens for distant vision and the lower half is a convex lens for reading.

items.stem: (i) Draw a ray diagram to explain the term angle of deviation. (ii) Why do the component colours of incident white light split into a spectrum while passing through a glass prism, explain. (iii) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the formation of a rainbow.
items.answer:
(i) When a ray of light passes through a glass prism, the emergent ray bends at an angle to the direction of the incident ray, and the angle between the direction of the incident ray and that of the emergent ray is known as the angle of deviation.
(ii) The splitting of the light ray occurs because of the different angles of bending of each colour: each colour passing through the prism bends through a different angle with respect to the incident beam (red bends the least, violet the most). This gives rise to the formation of the colour spectrum.
(iii) Rainbow formation : sunlight entering a spherical raindrop is refracted and dispersed at the first surface, totally internally reflected at the inner back surface, and refracted again as it leaves the drop, so the dispersed colours reach the observer's eye as an arc — red on the outside and violet on the inside of the bow. (Labelled ray diagram as shown.)

items.stem: A student finds the writing on the black board as blurred and unclear when sitting on the last desk in a classroom. He however, sees it clearly when sitting on the front desk at an approximate distance of 2 m from the black board. (a) Draw ray diagram to illustrate the formation of image of the black board writing by his eye-lens when he is seated at the (i) last desk, (ii) front desk. (b) Name the kind of lens that would help him to see clearly even when he is seated at the last desk. Draw a ray diagram to illustrate how this lens helps him to see clearly.
items.answer:
(a) (i) For the student sitting at the last desk the eye lens forms the image of the blackboard writing in front of the retina, so the writing appears blurred (figure). (ii) For the student sitting at the front desk, about 2 m from the board, the image is formed on the retina itself and the writing is seen clearly (figure).
(b) The student is suffering from myopia, so his eye defect can be corrected by using a concave lens of suitable focal length. The concave lens first diverges the rays coming from the distant blackboard, so that they appear to come from a nearer position (where the blackboard appears to be); the eye lens then forms the image on the retina and he sees the writing clearly even from the last desk.
